The '''NCR caravaner''' is a caravan driver for the [[New California Republic]] who appears in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Golden Rule]]===
This caravan driver from the [[New California Republic]] was captured by [[Hank MacLean]] and had a [[Brain-computer interface chip|mind-control chip]] implanted in the back of his head. Using the chip, Hank manipulated the caravaner into delivering a nuclear bomb to the former NCR capital of [[Shady Sands]] using a brahmin team, intending to blow up the city. Throughout the delivery, the caravan driver kept repeating the phrase, "Patrolling the Mojave almost makes you wish for a nuclear winter." Once the bomb was delivered, he began bleeding out, continually repeating the phrase "Mojave," and eventually died. [[Maximus]]' father [[Joseph (TV series)|Joseph]] discovered the chip in his head and then attempted to defuse the bomb, but was unable to do so. '''NCR citizens''' are civilians associated with the [[New California Republic]] in [[Los Angeles]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
These various civilians live and work around [[Griffith Observatory]], protected by the remnants of the [[New California Republic Army]] in the area. They include various [[human]] adults and children, as well as [[Freed ghoul|a ghoul]] whom [[Lucy MacLean]] from organ harvesters at a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] in [[Santa Monica]].

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Beginning]]===
[[File:Woman with flag.png|thumb|180px|left|One of the NCR civilians who joined the fight]]

When Lucy MacLean arrives at Griffith Observatory, she observes various civilians working in the walled courtyard, tending to the corn field, walking around, and sitting and eating food at a mess area. She briefly smiles when she sees two children run past, and she is also spotted by a ghoul she rescued from the Super Duper Mart, who is working the mess counter; the man next to him pats his back when this happens.

The '''news anchor''' is a character {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
The news anchor is a pre-War newscaster who was mainly shown reporting on current [[United States of America|American events]].

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The End (episode)|The End]]===
On the morning of the [[Great War]], the news anchor is seen on the [[Spencer residence|Spencer household]]'s [[Television|television set]], talking about the failure of peace negotiations between the United States and [[China]] at [[Anchorage]], [[State#Alaska|Alaska]]. He continued to talk about the specter of nuclear war which had faced the U.S. over the past ten years, but his broadcast was then turned off by [[Ronda Spencer]], who wanted to avoid bad news to focus on the party for her son [[Roy Spencer]].

===[[The Trap]]===
At an earlier time before the Great War, the news anchor is seen on television in a bar in [[Los Angeles]], talking about a shortage of [[uranium]] and increasing competition between nations over control of the resource. Because of this, the news anchor indicates that energy prices could surge in the upcoming winter, while also causing an expansion to the ongoing war. He tells his audience that his broadcast will continue after a word from his network's newest sponsor.
